general: The document |Must| describe the command-line interface of waterlint in a way that an LLM can use as a structured help source.
The document |Should| preserve the top-level command, global flags, subcommands, options, and option constraints.
The document |May| contain explanatory notes and examples, but those are secondary to the normative command structure.
requires: The top-level object |Must| define the command name, a usage string, and a list of global options.
Each subcommand |Must| define at least a name, a summary, a usage string, and an option list.
Each option that takes a value |Must| state that value placeholder explicitly.
Every non-trivial option relation |Should| be represented as an explicit constraint.
ensures: The reader can distinguish direct-object mode from replay mode for render-json.
The reader can see which switches are mutually exclusive and which options imply other options.
The reader can infer which arguments are required, optional, repeatable, or alternative forms of the same choice.
invariants: The top-level command name is always waterlint.
Subcommand names |Must| match the actual CLI subcommands.
Option flags |Must| be written exactly as they appear on the command line.
A constraint that uses an option name |Must| reference a defined option in the same command or at the top level.

global_options.summary: Show the top-level help text and exit.
Show the top-level help text plus all subcommand details.

notes: The top-level parser acts as a dispatcher to the subcommands.
Global help options are available regardless of the chosen subcommand.

Subcommands.name: validate
Subcommands.usage: waterlint validate [--basedir DIR] [--fail-on-warning] [--out-diag PATH] [--out-diag-json PATH] [--obj QUALNAME | --in FILE] [--debug] [--ignore RULES]

general: This subcommand |Must| validate either a resolved object or raw docstring text.
The diagnostics output |Should| remain optional and external to the validation result.
requires: The caller |Must| provide exactly one of --obj or --in.
When --obj is used, the object |Should| be resolvable from --basedir if the object lives in source code.
ensures: The tool reports warning and error diagnostics in a way that can be consumed by humans or machines.
The tool can treat warnings as errors when requested.
invariants: The meaning of --ignore is stable across validation invocations.

options.meaning: Base directory for resolving objects passed to --obj.
Treat warnings as errors.
Write human-readable diagnostics to PATH.
Write machine-readable diagnostics to PATH.
Qualified identifier of a module, class, function, or method.
Read docstring text from FILE instead of resolving --obj.
Emit debugging data to stderr.
Whitespace-separated list of rule IDs to ignore for warnings.

constraints.meaning: Use either object validation or text validation, not both.

Subcommands.name: coverage
Subcommands.usage: waterlint coverage [--fail-on-warning] [--out-diag PATH] [--out-diag-json PATH] [--basedir DIR] --obj QUALNAME [--ignore RULES] [--debug]

general: This subcommand |Must| assess coverage for a documentable object tree.
The object argument |Should| identify a module or class whose public surface is being audited.
requires: The caller |Should| provide --basedir when the qualified name is not already import-resolvable.
ensures: The tool produces coverage diagnostics that distinguish documented, under-documented, and missing docstrings.
The result can be used as a gate in CI.
invariants: Coverage is computed against the selected object tree only.
The warning policy is controlled by --fail-on-warning and the global diagnostics settings.

options.meaning: Base directory for resolving objects passed to --obj.
Qualified identifier of a module or class.
Whitespace-separated list of rule IDs to ignore for warnings.
Emit debugging data to stderr.

Subcommands.name: render-json
Subcommands.summary: Render Waterloo JSON from source or replay walk JSON.
Subcommands.usage: waterlint render-json [--fail-on-warning] [--out-diag PATH] [--out-diag-json PATH] [--in FILE] [--obj MODULE [MODULE ...]] [--basedir DIR] [--out FILE | --out-dir DIR] [--out-prefix PREFIX] [--flavour raw|rfc-2119|markdown] [--scope core|extension|public] [--include-imported | --no-include-imported] [--allow-local-paths | --no-allow-local-paths] [--debug]

general: This subcommand |Must| support two operating modes: direct source rendering and walk replay.
The output |Should| remain a single JSON artifact or a directory of JSON artifacts.
The generated document |May| contain local filesystem paths unless explicitly suppressed.
requires: Replay mode |Must| use --in and direct mode |Must| use --obj.
When multiple modules are rendered and --out-dir is used, the caller |Must| provide --out-prefix.
ensures: The tool emits a Waterloo JSON document with the expected structural markers.
The selected flavour and scope are reflected in the JSON metadata.
The resulting file name encodes the rendered object identity in a predictable way.
invariants: A walk JSON replay and a direct source render are mutually exclusive input modes.
The object identity used in the JSON tree is stable for the same import resolution context.
Imported-member inclusion is controlled only by the include-imported switches.

options.meaning: Read exactly one walk JSON file and replay it.
One or more qualified modules to render in direct mode.
Base directory for resolving --obj in direct mode.
Write JSON to FILE.
Write JSON into DIR with a generated filename.
Filename prefix used with --out-dir.
Normativity keyword flavour.
Render only objects visible in the given scope.
Include imported members and submodules.
Exclude imported members and submodules.
Include filesystem paths in JSON.
Omit filesystem paths in JSON.
Emit debugging data to stderr.

constraints.meaning: Choose either replay mode or direct mode.

Subcommands.name: render-html5
Subcommands.summary: Render Waterloo JSON to bundled HTML5.
Subcommands.usage: waterlint render-html5 [--fail-on-warning] [--out-diag PATH] [--out-diag-json PATH] --in JSON [JSON ...] (--out HTML | --out-dir DIR) [--css FILE] [--additional-css FILE] [--header-html FILE] [--pygments-theme THEME] [--no-render-preamble] [--allow-raw-object-node | --no-allow-raw-object-node] [--debug]

general: This subcommand |Must| transform Waterloo JSON into a single bundled HTML5 document.
The generated HTML |Should| remain self-contained unless custom assets are explicitly added.
The tool |May| render multiple JSON inputs in one invocation.
requires: The caller |Must| provide one or more input JSON files via --in.
The caller |Must| choose exactly one of --out or --out-dir.
The caller |Must| treat --allow-raw-object-node and --no-allow-raw-object-node as mutually exclusive.
ensures: The HTML output includes the rendered docstring tree for the selected object(s).
The header fragment, if supplied, can influence the visible title area.
The selected CSS inputs are embedded or appended in the output.
invariants: HTML output is derived from the JSON structure, not from raw source text.
The title and subtitle placeholders in a custom header are populated dynamically.
The output remains a single HTML file per invocation target.

options.meaning: One or more Waterloo JSON files.
Write HTML to a file.
Write HTML into a directory using a generated filename.
Primary CSS file to embed instead of the built-in default CSS.
Additional CSS file to append after the primary CSS.
HTML fragment file used instead of the built-in header markup.
Pygments style name for rendered examples.
Do not render section Preamble in HTML output.
Include collapsible section Raw object node in HTML output.
Exclude the Raw object node section from HTML output.
Emit debugging data to stderr.

Notes: This structure is intentionally close to the existing Waterloo docstring vocabulary.
The Contract blocks are only an experiment, but they demonstrate how an online-help JSON could carry normative expectations.
A future version could split each command into preamble, contract, options, examples, and constraints as separate typed subobjects.
